angle: READ THE PHOTO RIGHT (figure and ground). Work is in /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/read/: proposal.md, proposal.json, fig.js (the reading), run.js (the measure), board.js, src.js, page.html (a copy of the sb-levels HEAD 42fc8b19a page with a mask switch added in buildAt), boards/, and res-*.json and log-*.txt (the runs).
title: Figure and ground at capture, carried as a record v2 solid mask
pitch: When a photo is taken, find the wall and work out how its colour changes across the room. A cell is solid only where the photo looks different from that wall, so a darker lower wall stops swallowing the furniture. On 95 real photos this nearly doubles the rooms that build at the default box (15 to 29), and the box search drops from a median of 11 builds to 3. It does not make levels less filmy by itself: once the room is read correctly the wall is plainly empty, and repair still lays film straight up it. Build it in the same record v2 as the stepping stone repair and edge ledges, never on its own.
rules:
All of this runs at capture, on the crop at full resolution, using floats.
1. Take an area average of the crop at 96x192 (4x4 sub cells per grid cell) and convert it to CIELAB. For each cell keep its mean Lab and a texture value: the mean absolute step between neighbouring sub cells, counting L in full and a and b at half.
2. Find the wall. Smooth cells are those with texture under 5. Grow regions from them, joining 4 connected neighbours whose Lab distance (L weighted 0.5) is under 7, so slow shading stays inside a region and real edges stop it. Score each region by its size, with cells in the bottom quarter counting half. The best region is the wall. If it holds under 12% of the cells there is no wall: write no mask and keep the v1 reading.
3. Fit the wall's colour field: a quadratic surface in x and y for each Lab channel, fitted to the wall cells, then refitted twice after dropping cells whose residual is over 2.5 sd.
4. A cell that is not wall becomes solid when it departs from the field by more than 11 (L weighted 0.5) or has texture over 9. The exception is a cell more than 12 lighter than the field with little change of hue (window glass, a lamp, sky): it stays open, so a window becomes a solid frame round an open middle.
5. Ceiling: a smooth region that is not the wall and touches the top edge in 3 or more cells is open above row 16.
6. Floor (optional, tested as floorSolid): a smooth region that is not the wall and touches the bottom edge in 3 or more cells is solid below row 24.
7. Specks: solid or open patches under 3 cells flip. The core then runs its usual 2 majority smoothing passes, the frame rules and everything after them, unchanged. Turning that smoothing off was measured and is worse.
Two fixes the boards call for, not built: choose the wall only from rows 8 to 40 and refuse a region that mostly touches the top (r13 picked the beamed ceiling as its wall); and add interior ledges inside big solids (a bookcase reads as one block and its shelves are lost).
code:
- shell-capture: a new figure(crop) function of about 120 lines, run after fit and before the record is made. The capture oracle (tools/capture-oracle.js) and test/capture.mjs need the same step.
- core-record: v2 adds a has-mask flag and the mask, 1 bit per cell, row major, 144 bytes raw, through pack, unpack, the validator and encode. The share string grows from 779 to about 971 characters and the link from 814 to about 1006. The QR (byte mode, error correction L, measured with SB.qr) goes from version 20 to 23, 97 to 109 modules. Run lengths, or storing only the cells that differ from the v1 reading, would make it smaller; neither was measured. Double Exposure (mode 2) needs two masks (288 bytes) or keeps the v1 reading.
- core-pipeline buildAt: one switch. When rec.v >= 2 and the mask is present, solid starts as the mask instead of L < otsu(T); smoothing and everything after are identical. The prototype is page.html line 1336.
- Old share codes: v1 codes keep today's reading bit for bit, because the switch only fires on a v2 record that has a mask. The mask is stored, so the core stays deterministic and only reads bits. The cost is that taking the same photo again on another device may give a slightly different mask.

effort:
Three lanes, each about one lane day, built in the house style with a test and a redwatch row for every behaviour.
1. Capture lane (shell-capture, capture oracle, test/capture.mjs): figure() plus H-cap tests on painted fixtures (a shaded wall reads open, a cabinet reads solid, a window is a frame with an open middle, a beamed ceiling is not chosen as the wall, no wall gives no mask). 2. Record lane: the v2 mask field in pack, unpack, the validator and encode, shared with tonight's v2 biome byte. Round trip tests, a QR size test, and a check that v1 levelHash changes on 0 fixtures.
3. Pipeline lane: the switch in buildAt, with harness rows showing v1 unchanged and v2 deterministic.

risks: On its own it does not answer Stephen. Desert rows go from 44.7% to 54.3% on real photos and film share from 61.1% to 63.3%, so he will still see film going straight up.
Picking the wall fails on beamed ceilings and heavy clutter (r13, r04), and 21 of 95 real photos find no wall and fall back to v1.
The QR grows from version 20 to 23 (about 190 more link characters) unless the mask is compressed.
Capture is not identical across devices. Shared codes are safe because the mask is stored, but taking the same photo again can give a slightly different level.
Big solids lose their insides (bookcase shelves, the seat and back of a sofa) unless interior ledges are added, and those are not prototyped.
The timing was measured in Node on a loaded box, not on the Pixel.
calls: Build the new reading on its own now, or only inside the v2 that also has stepping stones and edge ledges? Options: (a) alone, which makes building easier but levels no less filmy; (b) bundled. Recommend (b).

What goes in the share code? Options: (a) the full 144 byte mask (QR version 20 to 23); (b) only the cells that differ from the v1 reading, run length coded (smaller, not measured); (c) the 18 numbers of the wall's colour field, with the core rebuilding the mask (smallest, but floats in the core put determinism at risk). Recommend (a) now, (b) later if the QR size matters.
Windows: a solid frame round an open middle, or fully solid? Recommend the frame with an open middle (a sill to stand on).
Floor: should a smooth floor read as solid ground (it builds more on the painted model, 45 against 37 of 63) even though it raises desert rows? Recommend yes, together with stepping stones.

title: Climb the photo: aim at the photo's own surfaces, never lose a room, clear away unused film
pitch: Right now most of a level is a ladder of film tabs up the wall. Where the bug stands is film 65% of the time on real photos and 73% on the painted rooms. If each repair pass aims at the nearest thing in the photo you could stand on (a desk, a shelf board, the top of a frame) and the edges of things are read as ledges, film drops to about half and the route crosses the room over the furniture. No room that builds today is lost. But in nearly half of every climb the photo has nothing to stand on at all, so the next big step has to come from how the photo is read, not from a cleverer repair.
rules:
Everything is gated on record v2. A v1 share code builds with today's rules exactly (opts.noClimb).
(1) Edge ledges (core-pipeline buildAt, after solid and plat are read, before landmarks). This is the investigation's (a), verbatim. wallSet = the two most common palette indices among open cells in rows 1 to h-2. A vertical cell pair (ia above, ib below) is an edge when all of these hold: neither cell is solid, ib is not wall paint, the indices differ, and at least one of: luminance differs by more than 30, S1000 differs by more than 350, or both cells have hue bands and the bands differ. A horizontal run of edges at least PLATFORM_RUN_MIN long becomes photo one ways on the lower row.
(2) Stepping stones (repair, each pass while the exit is unreached). This is the investigation's (e). topR = the highest reached row. The stone is the unreached standable cell above topR, not standing on a tab, nearest by Chebyshev distance to any reached standable cell, ties to the lowest index. That pass's stair aims at the stone. With no stone the pass does what today's does (the light, then the top rows, then the exit or the largest unreached mass). Up to 8 passes instead of today's 4. TAB_MAX 12 per pass and the 15% change cap stay. Every hop still comes from SB.reach.tables (FULL, MID, TAP), as in today's stair.
(3) Never lose a room (build). build() runs the v2 rules. If they refuse, it reruns today's rules on the same record and keeps that level (repair.wholeFallback = 1).
(4) Clear away unused film (proposed, not yet measured or timed). After the route is fixed, each tab pair the main ascent does not stand on is lifted one at a time. It stays lifted only if the exit, the reach share and the main ascent all stay valid. The boards show tabs nobody stands on in r03, o02, model-44 and the climbz version of model-41.
Rejected after measuring: my surface chain planner (Dijkstra over the photo's surface runs, with sideways bridges), a route score that charges film tabs, and a ZIG zigzag across the room.

title: Frame the interesting part: the game picks the crop box, his drag still wins
pitch: When he picks a photo, the game quietly tries a few hundred boxes across the whole photo. It ranks them by how much of the climb the photo itself would carry, builds the best few, and opens the crop screen on the best box that builds. On 28 real photos that box built 27 times; the centred box built 3. On the 21 photos where tonight's search also builds, the empty stretches of climb (desert rows) fell from 46% to 16% and the film share of the climb fell from 60% to 51%. The moment he drags, the box is his and Q96 ruling 3 works exactly as it does today.
rules:
1 Candidates (pure, in shell-capture): 1:2 boxes. Sizes start at fit.w and shrink by 0.7744 a step (two SEEK.SHRINK steps) down to the 192 px minimum. At each size, positions every quarter box in x and y, each clamped by C.clamp, duplicates dropped, the centred C.fit box first. That gives 351 to 356 boxes on a 4:3 decode of 1024 px and 833 on a portrait model room.
2 Cheap score Q, no build. The 24x48 grid comes from a summed area table over the decoded photo; it is byte equal to the capture oracle's area average (check.js). Each cell takes its nearest palette entry (cached), then pipeline A's reading runs (Otsu, smoothing, frame rows, edge one ways); this equals stage A on every box checked.
- Standing row: an open cell over a photo solid (not the floor row) or over a one way.
- Base: the standing row if it has an open cell, else the lowest standing row.
- Climb: from the base up to EXIT_ROWS.
- Desert: rows inside runs of more than JUMP_UP rows with no standing row.
- Things: solid components of LANDMARK_MIN or more cells, and no more than half the grid.
- Q = (climb - desert) + 2 x min(things, 4) - 2 x (rows short of FALLBACK_MIN_CLIMB).
3 Build in Q order (ties go to the larger box). Skip any box that overlaps a box already refused with IoU over 0.6. Stop when 4 boxes build or 16 have been tried.
4 Pick: among everything that built (the centred box, the scorer's builds, and tonight's seek from the centred box, run only when the scorer found nothing), take the highest post score: (1 - desert share) - 0.5 x the ascent's film share + 0.2 x min(1, climb/40).
5 Blank guard (not measured yet): never pick a box whose grid has 3 or fewer palette entries holding 2% or more of the cells, unless nothing else builds.
6 Screen:
- The crop screen opens at once on the centred box.
- The worker answers in about 0.4 s of CPU in Node. The box then glides to the pick with the line "Framed for you. Drag to frame your own."
- A drag or pinch at any time stops the glide, and the box is his.
- An "Another view" button (48 px) steps through the other built picks, up to 4.
- Develop on his own box keeps Q96 ruling 3: a refusal searches from HIS box.
7 The final build always runs on the real C.downscale of the chosen box. If that refuses, try the next pick, then today's search.

title: Film set pieces on blank wall: gallery, switchback, chimney
pitch: When a stretch of the photo gives the bug nothing to stand on, the game stops laying the usual diagonal ladder up the room's edge. It hangs one of three film set pieces there instead: a gallery of film frames, a switchback of film strips that runs across the room, or a wall jump chimney. The room's biome and seed choose which one. On his real photos this roughly halves the stair moves in the rooms that get a piece (41.8% down to 19.9%). The bot still clears every one of those rooms, and old share codes keep their levels.
rules:
Prototype: /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/blank/v3/pieces-core.js, injected into copies of the sb-levels page by v3/pieces.js. Everything below runs inside repair (core-pipeline) on every pass, before the stair.
1. The frontier and the target are found as today.
2. Desert test: going up from the frontier, count the rows that have no photo standing cell within 6 columns of it. A photo standing cell is an open cell over a photo solid that is not the floor row, or over a photo one way. Fewer than 6 rows: lay today's stair. 6 or more: lay a piece from the frontier up to ytop = max(target row, the desert's top, frontier row - 18, 3).
3. Piece order by biome:
   - Attic: gallery, zigzag, chimney
   - Frost: zigzag, gallery, chimney
   - Deep: chimney, gallery, zigzag
   - Overgrowth: chimney, zigzag, gallery
   - Ember: zigzag, chimney, gallery
   When ((seed + pass*2654435761)>>>3)%3==0 the first two swap, so one room in three leads with its biome's second piece.
4. Lay the piece, then commit it only if the reach graph from spawn reaches the piece's top standing cell. Otherwise undo every cell and try the next piece. If none fits, lay the stair. Every film cell follows the stair's tab rule: open, not on or beside a landmark top, never directly over or under another one way, and open space above it.
5. If repair with pieces ends in needsCrop, restore the photo's cells and run repair again with the stair alone, so no build is lost.
6. Gate all of this on record v2. v1 codes run today's repair untouched.

The three pieces:
- GALLERY: frames 3 to 5 cells wide. A frame's top edge is a one way ledge. Its body, the 2 rows under the ledge, must be open wall and is drawn as a film frame with no collision. Each next frame rises 3, 4 or 2 rows, after a gap of 2, 3 or 1 empty columns, on either side, in an order shuffled by the seed. The first candidate that passes the stair's own hop test against the reach tables is hung. At least 3 frames or the piece fails; at most 10.
- ZIGZAG switchback: legs 5 rows apart (6 in Deep, so a straight jump cannot skip a leg). Each leg is a film strip from column 5 to column 18 with a 1 cell sprocket hole every 6th cell. A 2 cell turn tab sits 3 rows above each leg's far end, and the next leg starts 3 columns back and runs the other way, so the player runs every leg end to end. Legs stay 5 cells off the room's sides: at 2 cells the frame edge became a wall jump ladder and the climb skipped the legs. At least 2 legs.
- CHIMNEY: a 3 wide interior around the frontier between two solid film walls, or one wall and the room's edge. The walls run from one row above the floor up to 14 rows. A 1 cell rest nub sits every 5 rows on alternating walls, because the route score allows at most 2 wall jumps in a chain. A 3 cell film cap closes the top. At least 6 rows or the piece fails.

title: Three stars a room, film cans on the photo's own surfaces, an album and photo quests
pitch: Every room gets three stars: light the beacon, find the film, and take no hit. The film is up to 3 cans that the game sets on the photo's own shelves and tops, away from the film tab ladder. A star pays only the first time, so a new photo is worth about twice a replay. An album keeps every room you climbed with its stars, and photo quests (a daily photo and three open quests) send you out with the camera.
rules:
FILM CANS (in core-features, the last step after settle, no rng draw). A spot is a standable cell that is reached from spawn (reach distances >= 0). The cell under it must be photo: a one way that is not a film tab, or a solid above the floor row. The spot sits at most spawn row minus 2. It is not the spawn, exit, chest, scroll, door, a speck, an enemy cell or a pocket cell. A surface is a maximal run of spots in one row, and its cell is the run's middle (the left middle when the run is even). off = the least Chebyshev distance from that cell to a standing node of the main ascent. Sort surfaces by off (largest first), then row (higher first), then index (lowest first). Take a surface when its row is at least FILM_ROW_GAP 6 from every surface already taken, and stop at CAP_FILM 3. Store the picks as level.features.film and append that to the level FIELDS.

SIM: LOOT_FILM 4 is appended after the blueprint. Touching a can takes it like a speck, draws nothing and pays nothing. No new state field.

STARS (at the clear and at the doorway):
- Beacon: the clear.
- Film: every can taken, or the room has none ('No film in this room').
- Clean: no EV.HURT from entry to the clear. A hit that Thick Skin absorbs does not count.
Best stars are kept per grid seed. Each new star pays STAR_DP 5 at x1 in every mode. No time star, because the page has no honest par.

ALBUM (save.album): every cleared room as {code, seed, biome, stars bits, film [got, of], first date, clears}, newest first, cap 300. It starts from recent, with the Beacon star only. The screen is a contact sheet headed 'Album 31 rooms, 64 stars', with five biome badges that light when an album room has that biome.

QUESTS (save.quests): three open slots filled from a fixed ordered deck, plus the daily photo. Checked at every clear and doorway. A finished quest shows 'Ready to collect' and a tap pays it.
- Deck v1 (ships now): Climb a new room 10, Find all the film in a room 15, Three stars in a new room 25, Climb three new rooms in a day 30, Find all the film in three rooms (a frame), Not a scratch in room 4 or 5 of a house 40, Clear a house with 10 stars or more (a frame).
- Deck v2 (after record v2 and the crop screen's 'Reads as blue' readout, which is B1 over the box's 1152 cells): a blue, a red and a white room at 30 each; 'Climb a green room. A plant or a garden works.' at 40; 'Rooms of every colour' for a hero skin.

DAILY PHOTO: prompt = FNV-1a(local date string) over the prompt list. It is done by clearing a room that is new to the album that day and fits the prompt. Pays 20 DP and keeps a streak; day 7 of a streak gives a frame. Before v2 the only prompt is 'A room you have never climbed'. Green comes up at most one day in ten.

STAR ROAD (Stephen's call): 10, 25, 50 and 100 stars each unlock a frame style. House clears keep giving hero skins (Q97).

SCREENS:
- Title, after the first clear: the house buttons, 'Houses cleared 2', a dashed 'Today's photo' card, 'Album 31 rooms, 64 stars', 'Photo quests 1 ready', Free play, Settings.
- In a room, the strip shows 'Film 2/3'.
- Clear card: 'Room cleared'; three stars 'Lit the beacon', 'Film 2 of 3', 'Not a scratch'; 'Banked 27 dead pixels'; '2 new stars, plus 10'; a hint for a missed can, such as 'The last film can sits on the high shelf on the left'; 'Quest done: Climb a blue room'; buttons 'Shoot the next room', 'Play it again', 'Album'.

title: Code the record and spend the saved bytes on a 2x2 detail layer: look only, levels unchanged, the QR never bigger than today's
pitch: Today's share code stores every cell as a raw nibble. Coded the way photos compress, the same room fits in about a third of the space. The bytes saved carry a detail layer of 2x2 sub pixels per cell, drawn under the same level lines, so you can see picture frames, window bars, shelves and book spines. Levels, seeds and old codes do not change, and the QR is never bigger than today's.
rules:
1. Record v2 packed form: header (v=2, w, h, mode, focal as uint16, biome byte, flags byte with bit 0 = has detail), then the coded 24x48 grid, then, when the flag is set, the coded 48x96 detail grid. The JSON form gains `detail`: 96 strings of 48 hex digits, index 15 refused as today.
2. The grid coder (ES5, integers only, no Math.pow). Each cell's colour is written as its rank in a candidate list: left, up, up left, up right (no repeats), then the indices 0..14 not yet listed. The rank goes through an adaptive frequency range coder: 15 symbols, counts start at 1, +24 per use, all halved when the total passes 65536. There is one table per context: how many distinct colours among left, up (and, for detail, the parent cell), and whether left equals up. The detail grid uses the same coder with its own cell's colour first in the list. My sizes are the ideal code length plus 2 bytes; a real range coder lands within a few bytes of that.
3. The byte budget, applied at capture only. Build the 48x96 grid with the capture oracle's area average and palette.nearest. 6. Readability guard, as a test row: at most 12 decoy runs per level on the fixtures. A decoy run is a horizontal light over dark step of 40 or more luminance, 8 px wide or more, inside an open cell and away from the cell's edge. 12 is the measured p90 for 2x2.
